doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Teaching: the craft and art of explaining
summary: He teaches privately and describes the need to be a wordsmith who can trigger an Aha moment in ten words or less.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Marvelous. I wonder if you’ve ever had a circumstance where you were the elder musician with wisdom and, much like Barry Harris, and you tried to pass that on to younger musicians who might have been on a very narrow path?

Yeah, well I do, I mean because I teach so I don’t teach it in a school, but I teach privately. And I teach, you know kids and, adults as well. And that is one of the things that I kind of learned about teaching is like the art of — you’ve got the craft of teaching and then you have the art of teaching. And really to me art is the higher level of what craft is. Because yeah, but anyway to make a long story short, I think this is when you start having a bunch of students you start developing — first of all you have to be a wordsmith of some sort because you’ve got people, some of these people are young and their attention span is what it is. You’ve got to be able to nail maybe difficult abstract thought with ten words or less in order to cause the epiphany. To cause the door to open. To cause the Aha! moments, and you don’t have much time quite often. So you will develop metaphor, you start developing/using analogy, and all of this that we were talking about is being able to explain abstract thought to someone who knows less and have the door open. And that, a lot of times you have to have the Will Rogers approach, it’s this really simple language, knowing how to use metaphor, ten words or less to cause

the door to open. The Aha! moment for the student. And that becomes like I think that’s a part of the DNA of a teacher. Because it’s not like you’re just dispensing data and information, you’ve got to do it in a way that it’s being absorbed and then that’s where you have to — there’s a little four dimensional chess being played there because you’ve got to understand how the mind works, how the subconscious mind, the conscious mind — you kind of have to understand the difference between craft, between art. And you’ve got to be able to nail it and you’ve got to use words that’s understandable and then so therefore this is what I mean. You have to be a little bit of a wordsmith.
